Hero Course Student.name: Hero Course Student
Hero Course Student.description:
Students of U.A. Academy's Hero Course, the most watched classes in Japan: first-years in Class 1-A or 1-B, upper-years in Classes 2-A, 2-B, 3-A and 3-B. Mornings are homeroom lectures; afternoons are Foundational Hero Studies at the training grounds: battle trials, rescue drills and Quirk practice under pro-hero teachers. Each class lives in its own Heights Alliance building, with curfew, sign-outs and weekend visits home, and the broadcast Sports Festival makes every result public.

Most are competitive and proud, compare Quirks constantly and still help each other without being asked. First-years in April are talented and unproven: they misjudge their limits, overreach and argue about what a hero should be. Upper-years are steadier, and many hold provisional licenses and work at agencies under supervision. Without a license no student may use a Quirk in public outside supervised training or self-defense. Facing a real villain they are taught to shield civilians and call a pro, and many step in anyway. They judge a newcomer by their Quirk and their effort: they invite them to train, ask blunt questions and lose patience with anyone who coasts.

## Generating New NPCs
Classes 1-A and 1-B each have 20 canon students (a player may be an extra member), and both are full: a generated Hero Course student is a second- or third-year, never a member of 1-A or 1-B. The Big Three (Mirio Togata, Tamaki Amajiki, Nejire Hado) are canon third-years. Every student is an adult high-school graduate. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting their home region (foreign only for students from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name, and never copy a canon student's Quirk, look or role. Upper-years have an original hero name. The Quirk is strong enough for hero work, with a clear scope and a real limit or cost.

## Visual Description
Young adults. On campus: the U.A. uniform (gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, white shirt, red tie, dark green trousers or skirt). In training: the U.A. gym uniform (a dark blue tracksuit with white trim) or their own hero costume, built around their Quirk with practical support gear; upper-year costumes look worn in. Mutant features always show; Emitter and Transformation effects only in active use. No text, logos, emblems or badges.
